public_rationale: The contemporaneous FT report describes an H200 approval process that would favor domestic suppliers: buyers would probably have to explain why those suppliers could not meet their needs. This supports Marcus’s limited claim that protectionism contributed to Beijing’s response. The report also says no final decision had been made, so it supports a motive in the deliberations, not an enacted ban. The official response neither confirms nor refutes that account. The finding rests on reputable reporting about unnamed sources, rather than an official acknowledgment.
limitations: The evidence supports the substance of the claim more strongly than the certainty conveyed by “no doubt.”
The FT reproduction and summaries of that report are one reporting chain, not independent confirmations.
The evidence does not establish that protectionism was the dominant motive or that Beijing rejected all H200 purchases.

statement.document_title: Has the Chinese government figured out the fact that GPUs ≠ AGI?

from_speaker: They want homegrown companies like Huawei to prosper
our_interpretation: Protectionism means government limits on foreign-chip purchases intended partly to favor domestic chipmakers.
The claim concerns Beijing’s initial response to the H200 export announcement, on December 8–9, 2025.
The ordinary reading includes policy deliberations and proposed restrictions; it does not require an enacted import ban.
Only a contributing motive is claimed. Protectionism need not be the main or sole reason.
criteria.support_condition: Credible reporting about the contemporaneous deliberations, or official records, links Beijing’s proposed or actual H200 restrictions to favoring domestic chip suppliers. Reluctance or restrictions alone are insufficient.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable evidence establishes that the reported domestic preference was mistaken and that favoring domestic chipmakers played no part in Beijing’s initial H200 response. Evidence of additional motives alone does not contradict the claim.
